title: Hidden for Centuries: Royal Crowns and Jewels Found in Secret Spots!
summary: Have you ever dreamed of finding buried treasure? In 2024, that dream came true in Lithuania! Workers found royal treasures that had been missing for decades—hidden in a secret spot under a cathedral. The treasures included three golden funeral crowns, a fancy scepter (a royal staff), a shiny orb, and sparkling rings with real diamonds, rubies, and emeralds. They belonged to King Alexander Jagiellon and two queens from the 1400s and 1500s. The story gets even weirder: the treasures were wrapped in old newspaper from 1939! Back then, World War II was starting, so people hid the crowns to keep them safe. Then everyone forgot where they were. For almost 85 years, the treasure was lost. But in 2024, searchers finally found the hiding spot. The crowns were fragile and damp, but experts carefully fixed them. Now you can see them in a museum in Vilnius, Lithuania. One crown was made for Queen Elizabeth of Austria. It's a masterpiece of early Renaissance goldsmithing—that means artists shaped gold into delicate, beautiful designs. A gold chain found on Queen Barbara Radziwill is so detailed it looks like lace made of metal. And a special medallion for Queen Elizabeth has a tiny coin inside with portraits of two kings! The gems are clever fakes: hollowed garnets painted red to look like rubies, and crystal doublets with red backing to sparkle like precious stones. But wait—there's more! In Poland, another treasure was found in the 1980s. Workers digging for a telephone line found a vase full of coins from the 1300s. Later, they found a gold crown that probably belonged to a Czech queen named Blanche of Valois. It's the only crown of its kind left in the world! The treasure also had gold pendants, rings, and a huge clasp with an eagle made of gems—sapphires, emeralds, and pearls. Experts think a king pawned the treasure to a banker to pay for his campaign to become King of the Romans. The banker hid it, but never came back. So the treasure sat underground for over 600 years! These finds are rewriting history. They show how royal families from Poland, Lithuania, and the Czech Republic were connected long ago. And they prove that sometimes, real treasure is even cooler than pirate stories.
why_it_matters: This story shows that history is full of mysteries, and sometimes lost items can be found again, just like when you find a forgotten toy under your bed—but way cooler!

background_read: Lithuania (a country in Europe near the Baltic Sea) has a long history of kings and queens who ruled hundreds of years ago.
The Renaissance was a time about 500 years ago when artists in Europe created beautiful works, like the gold crowns found in this story.
During World War II (a big war that started in 1939), people often hid treasures to protect them from being stolen or destroyed.
Article_Structure: WHO: King Alexander Jagiellon and queens from the 1400s and 1500s, as well as a Czech queen named Blanche of Valois.
WHAT: Golden funeral crowns, a scepter, an orb, rings, and other jewels hidden for centuries.
WHERE: Under a cathedral in Vilnius, Lithuania, and in the ground in Poland.
WHY: To protect them from war, or because a king pawned them and never came back.
